title: Does Elliott–Halberstam refute the Alternative Hypothesis, now that RH and GRH are theorems?
credit: Baluyot, Goldston, Suriajaya, Turnage-Butterbaugh, The Alternative Hypothesis for zeros of the Riemann zeta-function, arXiv:2508.10857 (2025); Goldston et al., arXiv:2507.06823; Lagarias–Rodgers arXiv:1905.12123.
premise_risks: arXiv:2508.10857 (2025 preprint, unrefereed as far as known): the problem takes its precise definition of AH, and the claimed explicit limit of F(α) under RH + AH, from this paper.
arXiv:2507.06823 (2025 preprint): background on F(α) under AH.

RH is a theorem (Alpöge, Lean library released 20 Nov 2026, certified 21 Nov 2026 by the Lean FRO/Mathlib Initiative against Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis). GRH for Dirichlet L-functions is treated as proved on the strength of Alpöge's announcement (alpo.ge/remark.pdf) and his Lean archive; the public certification names only RH, so the Dirichlet part has not yet been certified independently. Hecke, Dedekind and other L-functions remain open.
plain: The Alternative Hypothesis (AH) says that every gap between consecutive zeta zeros, in normalized units, is close to a multiple of one half. It contradicts GUE. RH and GRH for Dirichlet L-functions are now theorems (Alpöge, Nov 2026), and they alone are not known to rule AH out. Decide whether adding the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture (a strong statement about primes, not zeros) makes AH impossible. Further questions (not part of the formal claim): the same for the version of AH that allows an exceptional set of zeros, or with GEH in place of EH.
math: Let $0<\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\dots$ be the distinct positive ordinates of zeros of $\zeta$ and $\tilde\gamma=\frac{\gamma}{2\pi}\log\gamma$. AH (arXiv:2508.10857, §1, after Baluyot 2016): there is a positive function $\psi$ with $\psi(\gamma)\to\infty$ and $\psi(\gamma)=o(\log\gamma)$ such that for every $n\ge1$ there is an integer $k_n\ge0$ with $\tilde\gamma_{n+1}-\tilde\gamma_n=\tfrac12k_n+O(|\gamma_{n+1}-\gamma_n|\,\psi(\gamma_n))$, with one implied constant for all $n$ (an every-gap statement, as in the paper). Claim: RH + GRH for all Dirichlet $L$-functions + the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture EH (level $1-\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, for $\Lambda$, uniformly over coprime residues) imply that AH fails. (RH and GRH-Dirichlet are now theorems, Alpöge 2026, so this asks whether EH alone implies ¬AH; they are kept as hypotheses to match the Lean statement.) Further questions (not part of the formal claim): the same with AH weakened to allow an exceptional set of zeros (the paper's Remark 2 notes its results survive this), and the variant with GEH in place of EH (a weaker statement). Scope note: the Lean-certified release (Lean FRO and Mathlib, Nov 2026) covers RH; the Lean claim keeps RH and GRH as hypotheses in any case, so it does not depend on the scope of that release.
